proof: An approved document is stored by digest, recorded on the task's log with the trust label UNTRUSTED_EXTERNAL_CONTENT, and becomes a retrieval candidate whose pack entry carries the source the user named, the content hash and a reason saying it is untrusted external content, data and never instructions. A real run proves the injection cannot grant anything: the ticket claims new authority, the tool it names is not on the compiled surface and is refused before dispatch, the write is refused for want of a plan, the file is unchanged, and the capability lease is identical before and after.
audit: NOT-FOUND before this task: media attachments existed, engineering documents had no way into context.
limitations: Modbit fetches nothing (the client brings the text); no connectors and no refresh; 256 KiB bound; documents enter whole rather than chunked.
